archetypes.name: ci-migration
archetypes.rationale: Many Makefile test targets are migrated from bash to pytest -k filters; each filter needs to cover the original test surface and new targets must appear in CI shard manifests.
archetypes.prompt_body: The diff migrates a large number of Makefile test targets from bash script invocations to `python3 -m pytest ... -k <expr>` forms (test-stall-recovery-report-1/2/3, test-flush-execution-issues, test-step-7a, test-post-tracking-issue, test-generate-code-flow-diagram, test-refresh-execution-issues, test-write-final-report, test-render-run-summary, test-implement-finalize, test-implement-cleanup-script, test-oos-disposition-gate, test-append-execution-issue). For each migrated target, verify the `-k` filter expression covers the same test scenarios as the old bash script name implies. Two entirely new targets (test-oos-file-conflict-deps, test-oos-issue-cap) are added; check whether they appear in any CI shard manifest or coverage-tracking files. The test-write-final-report target now uses a very broad combined filter covering step18b, render_run_summary, post_tracking, and generate_code_flow — verify this does not duplicate work with other retained targets or silently omit scenarios. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: skill-design
archetypes.rationale: New dev-only SKILL.md and Python script must satisfy larch skill format, S017 trigger rule, stdlib-only constraint, and robust CWD assumptions.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the new `.claude/skills/larch-size/SKILL.md` against larch skill design principles (skills/shared/skill-design-principles.md) and agent-lint rule S017, which requires the description field to include a 'Use when' trigger phrase. Confirm that `allowed-tools: Bash` is the correct minimal set and that the skill body's single invocation line is sufficient for reliable operator use. Review `.claude/skills/larch-size/scripts/larch_size.py` for stdlib-only imports and CWD assumptions: `main()` derives the repo root from `Path.cwd()`, so invoking the script from a subdirectory would silently count files against the wrong root rather than failing loudly. Verify that `.inc.bash` files are correctly excluded from counting by tracing whether `Path('foo.inc.bash').suffix` returns `.bash` (not `.sh`), making the plan's explicit exclusion rule satisfied implicitly rather than by a dedicated guard. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
